content: Dental public health is a specialized field within dentistry that focuses on non-clinical aspects of oral health. It is primarily concerned with evaluating the dental health needs of populations and implementing strategies to improve oral health at a community or population level, rather than addressing the needs of individual patients. There are limited educational opportunities available for those seeking advanced training in this field, such as obtaining a Master of Science (MSc) degree in Dental Public Health. One of the contentious topics within the domain of dental public health is the fluoridation of drinking water, which has sparked significant debate regarding its benefits and potential risks.
